metadata.title: Proof-of-Policy (PoP): policy compliance certificates for LLM agent responses
metadata.description: Proof-of-Policy (PoP) checks that a delivered LLM agent response satisfies a public policy without putting the response plaintext into the delivered certificate, and without trusted hardware. The artifact covers the Python reference layer and the certificate/verification chain: policy compilation, salted policy commitment, Ed25519-signed certificates, an append-only ledger, and third-party verify_session. Reproduction scope: the Docker image runs 42 pure-Python tests; on a host, scripts/ops/reproduce_artifact.sh runs demo_all.sh in fast mode (host checks, no SP1 proof, 13 certificates) and then verify_session.py (RESULT: PASS, 11 checks). The repository additionally contains cloud results that are NOT part of the image and NOT reproduced by the fast path: groth16 (16/18 matrix points; 279-344 s and 29.7-35.1 GB per successful point; a real EU AI Act policy proved at 301.19 s / 30.07 GB / 1874 B, wrapper-only hiding, non-post-quantum); 6-rule core scale (4500 characters feasible at 181.66 s / 64.2 GB, 5000 characters OOM on a 90 GiB cgroup); measured guessing entropy k (Qwen N=50 all-unique k=5.644 bit, cross-model N=20 k=4.322/4.242 bit, with an explicit N-truncation caveat); policy-corpus inference (L2 evidence commitments are linkable: top-1 0.382 synthetic, 0.112 on real responses, dictionary attack 0.207); a real DeepSeek agent end-to-end session (19 certificates, third-party verification PASS, no SP1 proof); and a real semantic-classifier feasibility study that is explicitly demoted (recall 0.50%, F1 0.010, ROC-AUC 0.583). Boundaries that must travel with these numbers: core is not zero-knowledge; groth16 is wrapper-level and non-post-quantum; the composition binds derive(T_U) rather than the user-submitted x_U (weak form); 6-rule >4500-character and 6-rule groth16 are not available; the k experiment is capped by sample size N. Every number must correspond to the released git commit and to a specific result file (for example bench/results/scale-cloud.md, bench/results/eu_ai_act_proof.md, bench/results/scale-6x4500.md, bench/results/k_entropy_crossmodel.md, bench/results/policy_corpus_infer.md, bench/results/agent_e2e_deepseek.md, bench/results/semantic_feasibility.md), with the machine, binary digest, policy vkey and proof_mode stated. Do not compare numbers across machines or proof modes as if they were the same table, and do not mix pre-NFA-fix with post-NFA-fix binaries. This template intentionally contains no DOI: Zenodo assigns the DOI at publication time, and it must be filled in afterwards.

metadata.notes: Version 0.2.0-rc1 is the M6 draft snapshot of the artifact metadata; replace it with the release version at upload. Artifact scope: pure Python reference layer plus certificate/verification chain. Entry points: Dockerfile (docker build -t pop-artifact . && docker run --rm pop-artifact) and scripts/ops/reproduce_artifact.sh on a host. In the authors' environment the Docker engine was unavailable at the M6 check (2026-11-01), so the image was not built and no image size is reported; the default CMD was executed on the host with the same Python and cryptography versions (42 tests OK), and the host script completed with RESULT: PASS (13 certificates, 17 Python tests plus doc-link tests). See docs/blockers/M6.md and docs/blockers/A4.md. The repository baseline for this template is commit 1c1fc60; <FULL_GIT_COMMIT_SHA> must be replaced with the exact released commit. Acceptance evidence: 42 pure-Python tests (host-equivalent), demo_all.sh fast report, verify_session.py RESULT: PASS, and tests.test_doc_links. No SP1 proving is performed by this artifact. The license and creators fields are placeholders and must be completed before upload. The release_checksums field below is a publication checklist, not Zenodo metadata: fill it with real sha256 values at release time.
